BUS.G11.T3.CITIZEN.A1.title: Citizenship roles & responsibilities
BUS.G11.T3.CITIZEN.A1.description: The citizenship roles and responsibilities business practitioners perform: how citizens, through business, contribute to the social and economic development of their communities, the concept of the business community, and the role of business, civil society, NGOs and CBOs.
BUS.G11.T3.CITIZEN.A1.strand: T3 — Entrepreneurial success, citizenship, marketing & production functions
BUS.G11.T3.CITIZEN.A1.recovery_strategy: NGO = non-governmental organisation (independent, often national). CBO = community-based organisation (local). Business practitioners are citizens who can give time, effort and resources to develop their communities.

questions.question: The letters 'NGO' stand for a _________ organisation.
questions.memo: An NGO is a non-governmental organisation — an independent body, not run by the government, that works for a public cause.

questions.question: A CBO is a _________ organisation.
questions.memo: A CBO is a community-based organisation that works to meet the needs of a specific local community.

questions.question: True or false: Business practitioners are also citizens who can help their communities.
questions.memo: Business people are citizens too, and through their businesses they can contribute to community development.

questions.question: Which is a way a business person can contribute to their community?
options: Volunteering time and skills to a local cause
questions.expected: Volunteering time and skills to a local cause
questions.memo: Giving time, skills or resources to a community cause is a clear example of a business person fulfilling a citizenship role.

questions.question: Giving _________ and effort to a community cause is part of a business person's citizenship role.
questions.memo: Contributing time and effort to help others is a key way business practitioners act as good citizens.

questions.question: True or false: An NGO is simply a government department.
questions.memo: An NGO is non-governmental — independent of the government — even though it often works alongside it for public benefit.

questions.question: Sort each organisation into the correct type.

items.text: A national charity independent of government
A local soup kitchen run by neighbourhood volunteers
A street committee fixing a local park

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: NGOs are independent (often national/international) bodies; CBOs serve a specific local community; government bodies are run by the state.

questions.question: How can a business contribute to the social and economic development of its community?
options: By creating jobs, training people and supporting community projects
By keeping all its profit hidden offshore
questions.expected: By creating jobs, training people and supporting community projects
questions.memo: Creating jobs, building skills and backing local projects all develop the community both socially and economically.

questions.question: Build a 3-part explanation of why a business practitioner should contribute to their community.
questions.prompt: Build a 3-part explanation of why a business practitioner should contribute to their community.

options.text: Business practitioners should contribute because they are citizens with a role in their community
Business practitioners should contribute only if forced by law
Business practitioners should never get involved in their community
Their skills, resources and influence can address real local needs
Businesses have no resources that could ever help anyone
Communities never benefit from local businesses
A stronger community provides customers, workers and goodwill, benefiting the business too
Helping the community always destroys the business
Community development has no link to business at all

questions.memo: Claim: practitioners are citizens with a community role. Evidence: their skills and resources can meet real needs. Explanation: a stronger community also benefits the business through customers, workers and goodwill.

questions.question: The people connected to and served by a business make up its business _________.
questions.memo: The business community is the network of people — customers, staff, neighbours — connected to and affected by the business.

questions.question: What is the main role of a community-based organisation (CBO)?
options: To address the needs of a specific local community
questions.expected: To address the needs of a specific local community
questions.memo: CBOs focus on meeting the needs of their own local community, such as feeding schemes or local clean-ups.

questions.question: True or false: Contributing to the community can also improve a business's reputation.
questions.memo: When a business gives back, the community and customers see it positively, which strengthens its reputation.

questions.question: Sort each action into whether it is a citizenship contribution or not.

items.text: Sponsoring a local youth sports team
Dumping waste illegally to save money

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Sponsoring, volunteering and mentoring are contributions; dumping waste, overcharging and ignoring needs are not.

questions.question: Which is an example of an individual giving back to the community through business?
options: An owner mentoring local youth and offering work experience
An owner refusing to speak to anyone local
An owner hiding all business activity
An owner blocking a community project
questions.expected: An owner mentoring local youth and offering work experience
questions.memo: Mentoring young people and offering experience uses the owner's position to develop the community.

questions.question: Why can individual business practitioners make a real difference in community development?
options: They have skills, resources and influence they can direct towards local needs
They have no ability to affect anything
Only the government can ever help communities
Businesses are always separate from communities
questions.expected: They have skills, resources and influence they can direct towards local needs
questions.memo: Business practitioners control resources, skills and networks they can put to work solving community problems.

questions.question: Civil society includes _________ and CBOs that work for the public good.
questions.memo: Civil society is made up of independent groups such as NGOs and CBOs that act for the public good alongside business and government.

questions.question: A business owner gives staff paid time off each month to volunteer at a local clinic. How is this best evaluated?
options: It fulfils a citizenship role and can build goodwill, though it has a cost
It is pointless because only government should help
It has no possible benefit to the business
questions.expected: It fulfils a citizenship role and can build goodwill, though it has a cost
questions.memo: Releasing staff to volunteer supports the community and builds the business's goodwill, even though it costs some working time.

questions.question: Why is contributing to the community described as a responsibility, not just optional charity?
options: Because businesses use community resources and people, so they have a duty to give back
Because the law requires every business to donate half its profit
Because charity and responsibility are unrelated
Because communities owe businesses their support
questions.expected: Because businesses use community resources and people, so they have a duty to give back
questions.memo: Businesses depend on the community for customers, workers and infrastructure, which is why giving back is seen as a citizenship responsibility.

questions.question: How do business, NGOs and CBOs ideally work together for community development?
options: Each contributes resources and reach to tackle social and economic needs together
They compete to avoid helping anyone
Only one of them is allowed to act at a time
questions.expected: Each contributes resources and reach to tackle social and economic needs together
questions.memo: Business brings resources, NGOs bring reach and expertise, and CBOs bring local knowledge — together they can address community needs more effectively.

questions.question: A successful local manufacturer wants to act as a responsible corporate citizen. Which plan fits best?
options: Partner with a CBO to run a skills programme for unemployed local youth
Quietly cut all ties with the surrounding area
Stop paying wages to fund a billboard
Move profits offshore and ignore local needs
questions.expected: Partner with a CBO to run a skills programme for unemployed local youth
questions.memo: Partnering with a local CBO to build skills directly develops the community and reflects responsible corporate citizenship.
